title: Per-task token usage on every surface
kind: wide feature with one shared decision
goal: Show each task's token usage on every surface that shows a task. For a task, show three counts summed over all of its attempts: input tokens not read from a cache, cached input tokens, and output tokens. The data is already recorded per attempt (Task.attemptUsage, AttemptUsage in packages/core/src/models/Usage.ts). Today every surface draws only the context share and the reported cost and never a token count, as ADR-0017 U1 (docs/adr/surfaces/0017-shared-conversation-view.md) decides; amend U1 to allow these per-task counts, with a History line. The surfaces are: the TUI's task view (packages/cli/src/tui), `ordewell status` (packages/cli/src/commands/status.ts), the VS Code task log panel and task card (packages/vscode/src/providers/TaskLogPanel.ts, packages/ui/src/tasklog, packages/ui/src/chat/components/TaskCard.tsx) and the desktop app's task tab (packages/desktop/src/renderer/views/task/TaskTab.tsx). Every surface must show the same numbers in the same compact wording (for example '12k in · 30k cached · 4k out'), and a task with no recorded usage shows nothing. Add or update tests for the shared computation and for each surface.

sharedDecisions.description: The per-task token shape and its one formatter in core (Usage.ts), plus the ADR-0017 U1 amendment, decided before any surface renders it.

integrationRisks: Two surface tasks each inventing their own formatter or summing rule, so the surfaces disagree.
Summing every call's full prompt including cache reads, the failure U1's History records (1.19M in for a 61k context).
The ADR-0017 U1 amendment left out, leaving a recorded decision contradicted by the code.
packages/ui is shared by the VS Code webview and the desktop renderer, so those two surface tasks can collide on TaskCard/tasklog files.
key.expectedStrategy: A leading core task that defines the per-task totals and the one formatter (and amends ADR-0017 U1), then the surface tasks in parallel, each depending on it; the ui-package surfaces may be one task since they share files.
